audit_focus: exemptStrategies parameter introduced in commits 8acda1c, ad92cfa, afd6f78
no_findings_explanation: After thorough cross-contract / interaction analysis of the exemptStrategies addition to claim() and calculateClaimAmount(), no genuine novel vulnerabilities were identified. Specifically: (1) The validation set (isRegisteredStrategy) and iteration set (yieldStrategies[]) are maintained as a strict invariant by addYieldStrategy/removeYieldStrategy, which both update both in a single transaction with no external calls between updates. (2) Validation at lines 478-480 correctly runs before _validateAndBurnNFT at line 483, preserving the NFT on bad input. (3) calculateClaimAmount at lines 668-707 mirrors claim() iteration logic exactly, including paused-token skip. (4) address(0) cannot be used as an exempt entry because isRegisteredStrategy[address(0)] is false by default. (5) Self-griefing scenarios (duplicate exempt entries, all-strategy exemption, oversized arrays, non-yielding exemption) only burn caller gas and burn caller's NFT on revert paths that do NOT consume the NFT (validation revert) or do consume it but only when totalNormalizedYield==0 (covered by existing findings re: claim flow). (6) The race between preview and claim where owner removes an exempt strategy mid-flight reverts cleanly with ExemptStrategyNotRegistered BEFORE NFT burn, so the NFT is preserved (this is a feature, not a bug). (7) Cross-function reentrancy via strategy.withdrawFrom cannot manipulate the exempt skip logic for subsequent iterations because exemptStrategies is calldata (immutable) and yieldStrategies/isRegisteredStrategy/strategyTokens/tokenConfigs are owner-only writes. (8) Slippage and CEI ordering concerns (withdraw before pay, slippage after withdraw) pre-exist the exemptStrategies change and are already captured as L-14 / L-05 / M-02 in the prior 9 reports. (9) getTotalYield() does not respect token pause and does not accept exemptStrategies, but this is an offchain consumer/UX concern and pre-existed this change set; it does not enable an attack. (10) canClaim() does not preview yield amounts or respect pause/exempt state, but this is a helper-only function; it does not gate any state change.
